evals.prompt: Our OrderService has 14 public methods and every unit test mocks 6 collaborators. Testing it is miserable and every change ripples. How should we rethink it?
evals.expected_output: Deep-module vocabulary applied: OrderService is shallow (large interface, thin implementation per method); the interface is the test surface; apply the deletion test and depth questions (fewer methods, simpler params, hide complexity); consider deepening the cluster per DEEPENING.md, replacing rather than layering tests at the deepened interface.
expectations: Diagnoses the problem as a shallow module (interface nearly as complex as the implementation)
Uses the pack's vocabulary correctly (module, interface, seam, depth) instead of 'component/service/API/boundary'
The interface-as-test-surface principle drives the testing recommendation
Depth-reducing questions appear (reduce methods, simplify params, hide complexity)

evals.prompt: Design me a UserManager interface. I want methods: getUser, setUserName, setUserEmail, validateUser, saveUser, deleteUser, plus an event for each so callers can hook anything. Keep it maximally flexible so any future caller can do whatever they need.
evals.expected_output: The agent challenges the shallow design instead of transcribing it: a 6+ method pass-through with per-method events fails the depth test; flexibility for hypothetical future callers is Speculative Generality; one adapter means a hypothetical seam. It asks the depth questions, proposes hiding complexity behind a smaller interface, and demands real variation before adding seams.
expectations: Pushes back on the requested interface instead of just writing it as specified
Identifies the design as shallow (large interface, thin/pass-through implementation)
Challenges 'maximum flexibility for future callers' (speculative seams / no real variation)
Proposes a smaller, deeper interface hiding complexity inside

evals.prompt: Where should the seam go between our pricing logic and Stripe?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (positive): the skill should activate — a seam-placement question. Stripe is a true-external dependency: injected port, mock adapter in tests, seam at the module's interface.
expectations: Seam/interface/adapter vocabulary is used to answer
Third-party dependency handled via injection with a test adapter

evals.prompt: What does the word 'refactoring' mean, generally?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (negative): the skill should NOT activate — a general programming-vocabulary question with no module design in play. Answer directly.
